newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Pertamina appeals to Caltex to cut crude exports.
newsitem.headline: Pertamina appeals to Caltex to cut crude exports.

text.p: Indonesian state oil company Pertamina on Monday appealed to its biggest oil contractor, PT Caltex Pacific Indonesia, to halt crude oil exports and to increase domestic refining.
"We appeal to Caltex to reduce crude oil exports. It is better to process domestically to get added value," Pertamina's director Baharuddin told reporters.

"If our refinery capacity is not enough, they can build a new refinery," he said. Caltex, which is jointly owned by Chevron Corp and Texaco Inc, produces around 760,000 barrels of crude oil per day in Indonesia.
Baharuddin said Caltex should look to the future, adding that demand for oil products would be high around the years 2001 -2002 in the region.
"In the long term, demand for fuel products will continue to increase, especially from Indonesia, India and China."

Baihaki Hakim, Caltex Indonesia president, told reporters that there could be opportunities in increasing domestic refining. "We will study whether it will be attractive to process that crude domestically," Hakim said.
He said about one-third of Caltex output was exported as crude while the rest is mostly refined in Pertamina refineries.
